column1: # dcho golden test set for the Persian text-to-phoneme frontend.
# Format: 4 tab-separated columns, one sentence per line.
#   1. id        three-digit id, unique. A leading `?` marks a row whose
#                phonemization the author was NOT fully confident about;
#                those rows need human review before they are trusted as
#                ground truth. Everything else is asserted with confidence.
#   2. category  one of: ezafe homograph stress numbers zwnj arabic
#                foreign punctuation names general
#   3. text      the input, in normal Persian orthography (ZWNJ included
#                where standard, Persian-Indic digits, Persian punctuation)
#   4. phonemes  the expected output of the text frontend
# Lines beginning with `#` are comments and are skipped by the loader.
# Symbol inventory: exactly the one defined in dcho/text/phonemes.py.
# No symbol outside that inventory may appear in column 4 (enforced by
# tests/test_golden.py, which tokenizes every row and fails on any UNK).
# Register: neutral formal Tehrani Persian, as read aloud by an educated
# speaker. Written forms only (نمی‌دانم, not نمی‌دونم); no colloquial
# reductions (است, not ه; را, not رو).
# CONVENTIONS
# EZAFE
#   The ezafe linker is written as `-` appended to the word that carries
#   it, never as a separate token: کتابِ من -> `ket1Ab- m1an`.
#   `-` always encodes the /e/ of the linker. When the host word ends in
#   a vowel the linker surfaces as /ye/; the linking glide is then written
#   OUT EXPLICITLY as `y` before the marker, so that column 4 is a literal
#   segmental transcription and the ezafe stays machine-detectable:
#       خانهٔ من      -> x A n 1e y -   ->  `xAn1ey- m1an`      (= xāneye man)
#       صدای موسیقی   ->                   `sed1Ay- musiq1i`   (= sedāye musiqi)
#       دانشجوی پزشکی ->                   `dAneshj1uy- pezeshk1i`
#   Words whose spelling already ends in a consonantal /y/ (روی, پای) need
#   no extra glide: `r1uy-`.
#   Rows where NO ezafe applies are included on purpose; they are the other
#   half of the test and are just as load-bearing as the positive rows.
# STRESS
#   `1` is placed immediately before the vowel of the stressed syllable,
#   exactly one per phonological word. Words written WITHOUT a stress mark
#   are unstressed on purpose:
#     - monosyllabic function words: را به از در با بر تا که و هر
#     - enclitics, which never move the host's stress:
#       possessive/personal endings (ـم ـت ـش ـمان ـتان ـشان),
#       verb person endings (خریدم -> xar1idam, stress on the stem),
#       the indefinite ـی (کتابی -> ket1Abi, فیلم خوبی -> f1ilm- x1ubi),
#       the past participle ـه (رفته -> r1afte).
#   Stress rules applied:
#     - nouns/adjectives: final syllable (مادر -> mAd1ar, خانه -> xAn1e)
#       including the relational ـی (ایرانی -> irAn1i) and ـتر (زودتر -> zudt1ar)
#     - simple past/present verbs: last syllable of the stem
#       (رفتند -> r1aftand, آمد -> Am1ad, کردیم -> k1ardim)
#     - verbal prefixes می‌ بـ نـ take the stress
#       (می‌روم -> m1iravam, بنویس -> b1enevis, نمی‌روم -> n1emiravam)
#     - the copula written as a separate word carries stress (است -> 1ast)
#     - vocatives shift stress to the first syllable
#       (علی! -> '1ali, but علی آمد -> 'al1i Am1ad)
#     - in compound verbs the nominal element keeps its own stress
#       (بازی می‌کنند -> bAz1i m1ikonand)
# GLOTTAL STOP
#   `'` is written only where the orthography has ع or ء/ئ/أ
#   (علی -> `'al1i`, ساعت -> `sA'1at`, رئیس -> `ra'1is`).
#   A word-initial vowel spelled with ا/آ is written bare (امروز -> `emr1uz`,
#   او -> `1u`): its glottal onset is automatic and predictable, so writing
#   it would only add a symbol the frontend must learn to insert.
# DIPHTHONGS
#   Written as vowel + glide sequences, using the two glides the inventory
#   actually has: /ey/ is `ey` and /ow/ is `ov`. There is no `w` symbol,
#   and `j` is the affricate ج (IPA d͡ʒ), so `ej`/`ow` would be wrong here:
#       قیمت -> `qeym1at`   کی -> `k1ey`     حسین -> `hos1eyn`
#       روشن -> `rovsh1an`  چطور -> `chet1ovr`  فردوسی -> `ferdovs1i`
# BREAKS
#   Emitted only where the source text actually has punctuation, and
#   separated from neighbouring words by a space:
#   Text with no final punctuation gets no final break.
# id
